brief.summary_1line: Ravana mocks Nandi at Kailasa, attempts to lift the mountain, is crushed by Shiva’s toe, and earns the name Ravana after his world‑shaking cry.

image_candidates.scene_text: Ravana with ten heads strains to lift Mount Kailasa while Shiva calmly presses it down with a single toe as Parvati clings to him.
The dwarf guardian Nandi, yellow and black, stands before Ravana and curses that monkey warriors will one day destroy him.
Trapped beneath the mountain, Ravana screams in agony while gods in the sky scatter flowers and the worlds tremble.

deep.rich_summary: After defeating his half‑brother Kubera and seizing the celestial Pushpaka chariot, the arrogant Rakshasa king Dashagriva (later Ravana) travels in triumph until the vehicle halts at Mount Kailasha, where Shiva is sporting. Nandi, Shiva’s attendant, bars his way and is mocked by Dashagriva for his monkey-like form. In anger Nandi prophesies that monkey warriors will one day destroy the demon’s race—a mythic foreshadowing of the Vanara allies of Rama. Enraged, Dashagriva attempts to uproot Kailasha itself. Shiva effortlessly pins him beneath the mountain with a toe. After a thousand years of hymns and penance, Shiva releases him and grants him the name “Ravana,” meaning “he who makes the worlds cry out,” explaining the legendary origin of the demon king’s name.

highlight_spans.why: The opening description of the divine Pushpaka chariot sets the mythic tone and emphasizes Ravana’s stolen celestial power.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ravana strains with his many arms to uproot Mount Kailasha while Shiva calmly presses the mountain down with a single toe, trapping the demon beneath it.
Nandi, the stout dwarf attendant of Shiva with a monkey-like face and trident, fearlessly confronts Ravana before the sacred mountain.
The universe trembles as Ravana, crushed beneath Kailasha, releases a world‑shaking cry that echoes through the three worlds.
